extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: A large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies.

extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 16 publicly available datasets: MGH Wild, SOOP, BraTS-GEN, OASIS1, OASIS2, MSD Braintumor, IXI, NIMH, DLBS, IDEAS, ARC, MBSR, UCLA, QTAB, NKI, AOMIC ID1000
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MRI preprocessing comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. All scans were first reoriented to RAS and affinely co-registered using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.1, with default parameters. Within each MRI session, scans were aligned to the image with the highest spatial resolution to preserve anatomical detail. For diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) scans stored in 4D format, additional steps were applied. If a b=0 (non-diffusion-weighted) volume was available, it was extracted and saved separately. For the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on their gradient directions being most closely aligned with the canonical x, y, and z axes. Alignment was determined by computing the cosine similarity between each gradient vector (bvec) and the orthogonal unit vectors. The corresponding volumes were averaged to produce a single representative 3D image. Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1), which outputs segmentation masks of brain structures. These masks were used to define the brain extraction region. Skull-stripping was only applied when the images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features that could compromise anonymization.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Brain MRI scans, anatomical and pathological variability
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Minimal preprocessing was applied to preserve the original image characteristics while reducing barriers to entry for new users. In cases where sequence information is unavailable, scans are generically named scan_X.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale. Can be used with no further pre-processing for pre-training.
